Suppressed Menses Counseling: Advanced maternal age, patient apprised that women approaching or beyond the age of 35 have a greater chance than younger women of having a baby with a chromosome abnormality. The patient was counseled that genetic testing is not required but elective option. Discussed briefly the option of Harmony (cell-free DNA) prenatal screening for AMA patients, Harmony testing does not screen for all chromosome abnormalities, Harmony testing appears to be the most accurate screening test for Trisomy 21, false positive and false negative results do occur with Harmony. A negative Harmony result indicates indicates a decreased risk and does not rule out trisomy 21 or other chromosomal conditions. Diagnostic confirmation with information with CVS or Amnio is recommended for abnormal Hamrony results. If definitive information about chromosomal conditions is desired then CVS or Amnio with a referral to genetics is recommended
